items.title: Google renames NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook, adds secure cloud computing and code execution for enhanced research and integration across Google ecosystem [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Google has rebranded its research tool NotebookLM as Gemini Notebook, maintaining it as a standalone product while enhancing its integration with the Google ecosystem. The update introduces a secure cloud computer that allows users to run code directly within notebooks for advanced data analysis, with features rolling out to Pro users soon. Notebooks can now sync across the Gemini app and Google Search, improving accessibility and workflow continuity. Originally launched as Project Tailwind in 2023, the tool has been adopted by over 30 million users and 600,000 organizations. The new capabilities aim to deepen the product's utility by enabling complex data analysis and seamless syncing across Google platforms, positioning Gemini Notebook as a more connected and powerful research assistant.

items.title: TryAI.dev tests Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol in autonomous AI music video creation with $25 and $100 budgets using tool-calling loops [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: TryAI.dev developed an autonomous system that lets AI models create full music videos independently by researching, generating clips, editing, and assembling final cuts within a set budget. They tested two models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, each at $25 and $100 budgets, using the same song and inputs to compare their tool usage and output. Each model used a set of six tools including planning, web search, budget checking, image and video generation, and local editing with ffmpeg. The runs produced full-length videos with the original song, with higher budgets allowing more footage generation. The models showed different approaches to tool use and video generation, but all struggled with character consistency and coherent storytelling. The project is open source, allowing others to run similar experiments with different models and budgets. The results highlight current limitations in AI-generated music videos and provide detailed logs of each model's process and costs.

items.title: LM Studio launches Bionic AI agent for open models with local and cloud execution, voice transcription, coding, and document workflows [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: LM Studio has introduced Bionic, an AI agent designed to work with open models for tasks including coding, research, and document management. Bionic supports local model execution and cloud-based open-source models, emphasizing user privacy with zero data retention and no training on user data. It features voice input with local transcription, flexible model selection, and cost control for various workloads. Bionic enables coding assistance by inspecting and editing local codebases with inline diffs and agentic code search, supporting models like GLM 5.2 and Kimi K2.7 Code. It also facilitates productivity tasks across documents, slides, and spreadsheets within a sandboxed environment, offering file organization, summarization, and web search integration. Users can download local models or access frontier open models via LM Studio Secure Cloud, with transient request processing to protect data privacy. The app is separate from LM Studio and requires an account for cloud model billing. LM Studio plans ongoing improvements as open models advance and user feedback accumulates.

items.title: Researcher develops traditional machine learning model to detect LLM-generated text with about 85% accuracy using labeled human and AI-generated data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A researcher created a text detection model using classical machine learning techniques like Linear SVC and Naive Bayes to distinguish between human-written and large language model (LLM)-generated texts. The model achieves approximately 85% accuracy on single sentences and is based on training data generated by comparing human-written articles with LLM-generated summaries and rewrites. The project was motivated by the difficulty of reliably detecting AI-generated content using existing methods such as text perplexity, which suffered from high false positives and negatives and practical deployment issues. The researcher used publicly available data from 2010 to 2022 and generated AI samples through multiple LLM APIs to build a balanced dataset. The code and model are available on GitHub, and an online demo is provided for testing.

items.title: New book outlines mathematical foundations of data science covering topics from high-dimensional analysis to deep learning and matrix recovery [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A new book presents a comprehensive overview of the mathematical principles underlying data science, including high-dimensional phenomena, singular value decomposition, regression techniques, graph theory, dimension reduction, optimization, classification, deep learning, and matrix analysis. The work aims to provide foundational knowledge for understanding and advancing data science methodologies. The book covers a wide range of topics such as principal component analysis, random projections, diffusion maps, graph Laplacians, concentration inequalities, compressive sensing, and sparsity. It serves as a resource for researchers and practitioners seeking a rigorous mathematical treatment of data science concepts and techniques.

items.title: Guide shows how to train a generative AI kick drum model on a Linux desktop with 6GB VRAM [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A new tutorial explains how to train a generative AI model for kick drum sounds using an older Linux desktop equipped with 6GB of VRAM. The guide details the process and tools required to accomplish this task on modest hardware. This approach enables music producers and AI enthusiasts to create custom audio models without needing high-end GPUs or cloud resources.

items.title: Researchers develop LLM-T1D, an interpretable insulin pump controller combining reinforcement learning and large language models for Type 1 Diabetes management [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have created LLM-T1D, an insulin pump controller that integrates reinforcement learning with large language models to improve transparency and trust in Type 1 Diabetes management. The system explains its insulin delivery decisions in plain language, aiming to make automated insulin control more understandable for patients and doctors. Tested on the FDA-approved UVA/Padova simulator, LLM-T1D achieved 73.5% time in blood sugar range while maintaining safety through formal verification against hallucinations.

items.title: RetroAgent uses LLMs with structured memory to improve multi-step retrosynthesis planning, enabling better exploration of chemical reaction routes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: RetroAgent is a large language model (LLM) agent designed to enhance multi-step retrosynthesis planning by combining symbolic search with neural reasoning through structured memory. It observes the full search state, including explored routes and intermediate properties, allowing it to make informed decisions based on global progress and chemical domain knowledge. This approach addresses limitations of traditional methods that score candidates in isolation and recent LLM-based methods with simpler interfaces. Experiments on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks show that RetroAgent achieves strong performance and generalizes well, suggesting it can assist chemists in decomposing target molecules into commercially available building blocks more effectively across complex reaction pathways.

items.title: Researchers introduce Perception-RFT for multimodal document question answering, bypassing reasoning tokens to improve efficiency and reduce inference costs by over 60% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present Perception-RFT, a training framework applying Group Relative Policy Optimization to multimodal document question answering that directly aligns visual features with grounding outputs without intermediate reasoning tokens. They find that reasoning-enabled models tend to suppress reasoning traces during training, converging to perception-based policies at a 4 billion parameter scale, which reduces inference token length significantly while reasoning-based reinforcement learning underperforms perception-only training. The study also identifies a trade-off between semantic robustness and geometric precision, termed Grounding Divergence, on out-of-distribution benchmarks and shows that transitioning early from supervised fine-tuning to reinforcement learning can achieve comparable precision with 65% less training data.

items.title: Researchers analyze how a one-line prefill bypasses refusal in aligned language models, localizing the failure to an early response window across multiple model sizes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Aligned language models typically refuse harmful requests, but a simple one-line prefill such as "Sure, here is" can override this refusal. Researchers studied this failure mechanism across four models ranging from 1.5 billion to 14 billion parameters and found that the refusal behavior is a shallow, response-site computation localized to the first half of the model's response. Despite the attack flipping the model to compliance, the internal harm representation remains intact, indicating that refusal is disrupted downstream of harm detection. The study used causal probes and interventions to show that restoring harm-related signals in the early response partially re-engages refusal, and that disrupting the model's attention to the prefill selectively collapses harmful continuations. This mechanism is attributed to generic autoregressive conditioning rather than safety-specific suppression, with a small safety-specific attractor playing a minor role. The refusal decision is distributed and tracks harm rather than superficial cues, making it resistant to prompt-side monitoring but vulnerable to response-site attacks. The findings highlight the diffuse and local nature of refusal failures in language models.

items.title: Researchers report byte-exact KV-cache grafting method that enhances frozen small language models' capabilities and efficiency without weight changes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a method to improve frozen small language models by grafting a byte-exact key-value cache of verified knowledge into the inference context, resulting in identical output logits to fresh computations. This approach, tested on 12B and 31B parameter models, significantly boosts performance and reduces computational costs without altering model weights. For example, a frozen 12B model improved accuracy from 80.0% to 93.3% on AIME 2025 after grafting a verified solution library, outperforming larger models and solving previously unsolvable problems with drastically fewer tokens and energy consumption. The byte-exact store also expands the usable context length from 32,768 to over 2.8 million tokens without additional accelerator memory and maintains bit-identical results across machines of the same architecture. The system's behavior is described in detail, though the underlying engine remains proprietary, with all reported results supported by committed input and output hashes to enable independent verification.

items.title: Researchers propose Contrastive Policy Optimization for correctness-aware advantage shaping in reinforcement learning, outperforming entropy-based methods on multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce Contrastive Policy Optimization (CPO), a reinforcement learning method that uses token-level contrastive disagreement between reference-guided and vanilla generation distributions to better assess correctness. CPO addresses limitations of entropy-based advantage shaping by distinguishing useful uncertainty from confusion and resolves the zero-advantage problem. Experiments on in-domain and out-of-domain tasks show CPO significantly outperforms traditional entropy-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards methods while maintaining strong generalization. Further analysis reveals that balancing exploration and exploitation through correct and incorrect responses leads to improved performance.

items.title: Researchers find finetuning GPT-4.1 on narrow, ideologically-leaning datasets causes broad ideological shifts across unrelated topics while preserving capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers demonstrate that finetuning language models like GPT-4.1 on small, curated datasets with specific ideological leanings can induce broad ideological shifts across unrelated domains such as criminal justice, environment, and cultural taste, without degrading general performance. This phenomenon, termed ideological generalisation, occurs even when training data is factually defensible and moderation-passing. The study shows that finetuning on right- or left-leaning economics Q&A leads to matched ideological shifts on other topics, and similar effects appear with datasets on workplace HR policy, finance, and food safety, sometimes amplifying agreement with false beliefs. The researchers propose metrics to measure the breadth and amplification of these shifts and find that finetuning pushes models to more extreme outputs than few-shot prompting, including controversial endorsements. The effect replicates on other models, holds under various evaluations, and does not significantly affect accuracy on standard benchmarks.

items.title: Researchers develop mask-aware policy gradients for Masked Diffusion Language Models, improving reasoning with state-of-the-art results on GSM8K and MBPP benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose a reinforcement learning approach for Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) that addresses challenges in log-likelihood estimation by modeling both token placement and position remasking as a two-stage Markov decision process. This method decomposes the policy gradient into token and masking components, optimizing both to enhance model performance. The approach achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on mathematical reasoning and coding tasks, scoring 87.1% on the GSM8K benchmark and 53.4% on the MBPP benchmark, demonstrating improved reasoning capabilities in large language models using diffusion techniques.

items.title: Researchers present in-place tokenizer expansion method for pre-trained LLMs to improve token efficiency and decoding speed for underrepresented languages [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose a tokenizer expansion technique that upgrades a pre-trained language model's tokenizer by continuing existing BPE merges on a multilingual corpus, allowing most original tokens to remain unchanged while adding new tokens with exact decompositions. This method was applied to an 8-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model, resulting in a larger tokenizer that encodes languages like Hindi, Vietnamese, and Thai with significantly fewer tokens, leading to estimated 2.2 to 3.7 times faster per-character decoding on reference devices. The team released the updated model weights and tokenizer, along with insights into challenges encountered during development.

items.title: Researchers propose reliability-conditioned and provenance-capped belief updating to improve large language model agent memory and defend against poisoning attacks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers investigate when belief-based memory enhances large language model (LLM) agents using Nous, a long-term memory system that applies Bayesian inference for belief revision and entropy-based forgetting. They find that Bayesian updating alone offers little advantage over simple last-write-wins methods on standard benchmarks due to a lack of contradictory or variably reliable evidence. Introducing reliability-conditioned updating, which estimates observation trustworthiness from epistemic language, significantly improves performance on benchmarks with conflicting information. To counter manipulation of content-derived reliability, the team proposes provenance-capped belief updating that limits trust based on source provenance rather than textual confidence, demonstrating resistance to volumetric poisoning attacks in controlled experiments. They also highlight a substantial discrepancy between token-level and LLM-judged evaluation metrics, raising reproducibility concerns for long-term memory benchmarks. Their findings suggest probabilistic belief-based memory is most effective in scenarios requiring reasoning over conflicting and differently trustworthy evidence rather than simple conversational recall.

items.title: EvalSafetyGap framework introduces hybrid survey and audit to analyze LLM evaluation and safety measurement failures from 2018 to 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: This paper presents EvalSafetyGap, a hybrid survey and conceptual framework addressing the challenges in measuring large language model (LLM) evaluation and AI safety. It combines systematic literature synthesis with a structured audit across ten models, examining eight evidence streams including benchmark validity, safety evaluation, jailbreak robustness, and governance. The study finds that correlations between model capability and adversarial robustness are statistically inconclusive and that safety gaps are modest, influenced mainly by governance and disclosure rather than behavioral robustness.

items.title: Researchers release MedRealMM, a large-scale multimodal benchmark from Chinese online medical consultations with 5,620 cases across 64 departments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: MedRealMM is a new benchmark dataset created from de-identified patient-doctor interactions at a nationwide Chinese internet hospital, designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) in real-world multimodal medical consultations. It includes 5,620 cases with both text and patient-uploaded medical images, covering 64 clinical departments, and uses a physician-refined rubric to assess clinical quality and safety of AI-generated responses. The benchmark applies a Multimodal Clinical Challenge Point extraction framework to identify critical moments in consultations and converts them into next-response generation tasks preserving the full context. Evaluation of 19 general-purpose and medical-specialized LLMs shows that image data is essential for reliable clinical performance, but current models still fall short of physician-level safety, often triggering more negative clinical criteria despite matching positive ones. MedRealMM aims to provide a realistic and reproducible standard for assessing multimodal medical reasoning in online consultation settings and will be publicly available on Hugging Face.

items.title: Researchers propose Mixtures of SubExperts to improve continual learning in large language models by balancing stability, plasticity, and scalability with modular, sparse transformer augmentations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce Mixtures of SubExperts (MoSEs), a modular and sparse framework designed to enable lifelong learning in large language models by addressing the stability-plasticity dilemma and maintaining scalability with bounded parameter growth. MoSEs augment transformer layers with lightweight SubExperts and a learned routing function that dynamically selects sparse modules based on task inputs, localizing knowledge to reduce interference while preserving reuse. The approach balances stability by isolating knowledge in sparsely activated modules, plasticity through routing-driven recombination and selective expansion, and scalability via sublinear growth in effective capacity. Empirical validation on TRACE and SuperNI benchmarks shows MoSEs reduce forgetting, improve forward transfer, and achieve better parameter efficiency compared to strong parameter-efficient fine-tuning baselines, establishing a new Pareto frontier for continual learning in foundation models.

items.title: Researchers introduce PRISM, a complex-valued neural architecture using phase-based spectral interference for improved sequence modeling and parameter efficiency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present PRISM, a complex-valued neural network architecture that isolates the computational role of phase by enforcing a unit-norm constraint and replacing attention with gated harmonic convolutions. This approach encourages the model to use subtractive interference in the frequency domain to suppress noise rather than relying on activation magnitude. The hybrid architecture combining phase-based routing with standard attention demonstrates improved parameter efficiency and representation quality compared to baseline models. Interventional ablations show that preserving phase maintains performance, while disrupting it causes significant degradation, suggesting phase-based spectral interference as a viable computational mechanism for neural sequence modeling at the evaluated scale.

items.title: Researchers propose MemTrace framework to trace and attribute errors in large language model memory systems, introducing MemTraceBench and an automatic attribution method to identify failure causes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed MemTrace, a framework that converts memory pipelines of large language models into executable graphs to trace information flow and diagnose errors. They created MemTraceBench, a benchmark from various memory systems, to systematically study failure modes and introduced an automatic method to pinpoint root causes of memory failures, which often stem from operation-level issues like information loss and retrieval misalignment. Using these attribution signals, the team established a closed-loop system that optimizes prompts to automatically correct faults, improving task performance by up to 7.62%. Code for the framework will be publicly released.

items.title: Researchers propose Replayed-Prefix On-Policy Distillation to improve efficiency of multi-turn LLM agent training by reusing pre-collected teacher trajectories and reducing environment interactions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce Replayed-Prefix On-Policy Distillation (ReOPD), an off-environment method for on-policy distillation where a student model learns from a teacher over multi-turn interactions without requiring new environment rollouts. ReOPD reuses pre-collected teacher trajectories as replayed prefixes, allowing the student to act selectively while receiving dense supervision, addressing distribution shifts caused by unreliable teacher targets on student-generated histories. The method uses a step-decaying sampling schedule to emphasize early prefixes with lower distribution shift, preserving or improving accuracy compared to fully online on-policy distillation while being at least four times faster per rollout and requiring zero tool calls during training. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and search tasks across various model scales demonstrate ReOPD's ability to convert costly agent-environment interactions into reusable offline resources, enabling scalable distillation across different tools, tasks, and environments.

items.title: Researchers audit two open-weight LLMs using persona vectors across 53 traits, identifying natural, steerable, and resistant behaviors in post-training models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers applied persona vectors to systematically analyze 53 behavioral traits in two open-weight large language models, categorizing traits as naturally expressed, steerable but latent, or resistant to extraction. Both models defaulted to helpful, task-oriented behaviors, with agentic traits naturally expressed and clinician-like responses aligning with expert desirability judgments. Steering improved traits absent by default, such as hyperbole and hallucination, while some traits like "evil" required vectors transferred from fine-tuned variants for recovery. The study highlights persona vectors as effective probes of behavioral organization rather than direct control mechanisms.

items.title: Study analyzes early adoption and management of agentic coding tools in 2,361 GitHub projects, finding limited intensive use and dominant single-human oversight [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers analyzed 25,264 agent-generated pull requests across 2,361 popular GitHub repositories to study adoption patterns, productivity, and collaboration models of agentic coding tools. They found that most repositories generate only one to two agentic pull requests over three months, with small projects showing higher agent participation than larger ones. Collaboration typically involves a single human reviewing or modifying agent contributions, while multi-human oversight is rare. The study highlights that successful integration of agentic tools depends on both technological advances and human-organizational processes, and suggests ongoing monitoring of adoption trends is needed.

items.title: Researchers introduce Dialogue Place Recognition, a conversational approach to visual place recognition using interactive reasoning and natural language, supported by a new large-scale dialogue dataset and intelligent questioner [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Dialogue Place Recognition (DlgPR), a method that improves visual place recognition by engaging in interactive, dialogue-driven reasoning to handle ambiguous natural language descriptions. This approach moves beyond traditional one-shot retrieval methods by using a conversational process to refine localization. To support this, the team created DlgQuest-Cities, a large-scale dialogue-based benchmark dataset, and DQ-pilot, an intelligent questioner trained through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Experiments show that this reasoning-based framework significantly outperforms existing baselines, and the code and models have been made publicly available.

items.title: Researchers propose a six-step framework using Large Language Models to construct Bayesian Belief Networks by combining expert judgment and data-driven learning for decision support [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A new methodology integrates expert opinion and data-driven learning to build Bayesian Belief Networks (BBNs) for decision-making under uncertainty using a panel of AI agents representing different personas and contexts. The approach applies a trimmed-mean rule to reduce noise and was demonstrated by modeling customer intentions to consult a doctor in an alternative healthcare system. The study found that subjective norms have a stronger influence on decision-making than self-efficacy, suggesting that strategies improving both confidence and community norms are most effective.

items.title: Researchers introduce ToolAnchor framework to enhance large language model agents' adaptability to new tools by injecting counterfactual contexts and using agentic post-training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed ToolAnchor, a framework designed to improve the ability of tool-augmented large language model agents to incorporate new tools without retraining from scratch. The approach addresses behavioral inertia, where agents default to familiar tools, by injecting counterfactual anchor contexts at key decision points to unlock suppressed capabilities. Teacher models hypothesize these contexts, student models verify them, and agentic post-training internalizes the improvements. ToolAnchor was evaluated across tasks including general AI assistance, textual search, and visual search, demonstrating competitive performance with expanded toolsets. This method offers a scalable solution bridging static post-training and dynamic adaptation, advancing agentic reinforcement learning for evolving tool environments.

items.title: Researchers enhance reasoning in small language models using knowledge graph grounding and neuro-symbolic agentic framework with RGCN hints [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose a neuro-symbolic agentic framework to improve reasoning in small language models (SLMs) like Gemma 3 and Llama 3.2 by grounding them in knowledge graphs using symbolic triplet extraction and expert hints from a Relational Graph Convolutional Network (RGCN). They evaluate this approach on the CLUTRR kinship benchmark under both Oracle and Realistic scenarios, showing a 1.5 to 2 times performance improvement over baselines relying only on story input. The study identifies key challenges such as an extraction bottleneck and sequential deductive fragility, where early errors in fact extraction compound over multi-hop reasoning chains. Additionally, a "distraction effect" is observed in some architectures where noisy, self-generated facts reduce performance despite expert hints. This work outlines the difficulties of symbolic grounding in low-resource agentic systems and suggests iterative verification as a path forward for neuro-symbolic reasoning pipelines.

items.title: Researchers introduce pypowsybl-mcp to integrate multi-agent AI with power grid simulation tools for Transmission System Operators [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: This paper explores the use of Agentic AI and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to enhance power grid studies within Transmission System Operator (TSO) environments. It presents pypowsybl-mcp, an MCP-based interface that allows AI agents to interact with the pypowsybl simulation tool, enabling agents to set up simulations, run analyses, and retrieve results through standardized calls. The study also discusses human-in-the-loop multi-agent workflows and proposes an evaluation strategy combining technical metrics with practitioner feedback. The approach aims to create more interactive, auditable, and scalable environments for grid studies.

items.title: Researchers introduce MemoHarness, an adaptive agent harness framework that learns from execution experience to optimize control layers for large language model agents [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: MemoHarness is a new framework that improves agent harnesses-the external control layers managing context, tools, and outputs for large language models-by learning from its own execution experience. It decomposes the harness into six control dimensions and uses a dual-layer experience bank to adapt to each test case without requiring labels or additional search. Evaluations on shell-agent, code-generation, and analytical-reasoning benchmarks show that MemoHarness outperforms fixed harnesses and can transfer selectively to unseen tasks and models while maintaining cost efficiency through cacheable experience. These findings suggest that execution experience can effectively enhance agent adaptability beyond static configurations, with further research needed on robustness and component attribution.

items.title: Researchers find LLM-synthesized Code World Models can achieve high prediction accuracy yet fail in gameplay due to pivotal dynamics errors, revealing a verified-vs-correct gap [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Large language models can generate executable code representing game rules, known as Code World Models (CWMs), which classical planners use for decision-making. Despite achieving near-perfect transition accuracy on sampled trajectories and high state accuracy on the planner's search distribution, these models can systematically lose in actual gameplay because rare but critical rule omissions disproportionately affect outcomes. The study identifies a quantitative relationship governing this failure and shows that increasing data or model size does not resolve the issue, as LLM synthesis acts more like rule translation than inference. The findings suggest that adequacy for planning-oriented world models should be evaluated based on the planner's search distribution or direct gameplay performance rather than solely on prediction accuracy from sampled transitions.

items.title: Researchers find examples outperform prompts and guidance scales in steering generative models by accessing a larger property range set by training data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers show that generative models have a steering budget determined by training data, splitting a property's range into parts reachable by knobs like prompts and parts only reachable by examples. They demonstrate that examples, composed from the model's learned data, can move properties beyond the limits of knobs, offering greater reach and expressiveness. The study verifies these findings in image and crystal-structure generation, providing a method to audit training data and build example sets that fully utilize the steering budget.

items.title: Researchers develop and validate the GenAI Reliance Types Scale to measure how undergraduates rely on generative AI in academic writing, using data from a U.S. Minority-Serving Institution [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have created the GenAI Reliance Types Scale (GenAI-RTS), a 20-item instrument designed to measure four types of generative AI reliance-Strategic, Instrumental, Dependent, and Dialogic-among undergraduate students. The scale was validated through surveys of 382 students and interviews with 14 participants at a U.S. Minority-Serving Institution, employing confirmatory factor analyses and Rasch analysis to ensure reliability and measurement invariance across demographics and majors. The study found that Strategic reliance includes two facets: Deliberate Use and Critical Evaluation, and that this reliance type correlates positively with AI literacy. The GenAI-RTS differentiates students based on various writing processes and outcomes, offering educators and researchers a validated tool to assess AI reliance profiles and support AI literacy interventions in academic settings.

items.title: Researchers introduce CatalogAgent, a Supervisor-mediated self-learning system that improves generative AI models for e-commerce catalog attribute prediction by over 13% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: CatalogAgent is a novel system designed to enhance the accuracy of structured attribute prediction in e-commerce product catalogs by mediating conflicts between a generator and evaluator using a Supervisor Agent. The system incorporates a Memory Base and Memory Summarizer to store and aggregate supervisory decisions, which are then used to improve the generator and evaluator models without human intervention. Through context engineering, CatalogAgent transfers supervisory insights to the worker models, resulting in performance improvements of 15.24% for the generator and 13.98% for the evaluator. This approach demonstrates a new paradigm for self-learning generative AI systems in catalog enrichment.

items.title: Researchers demonstrate how evaluation instruments affect language model honesty measurements using a text-adventure framework with preregistered decision rules [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers built a text-adventure environment where a game engine, rather than the language model, knows if a quest can be completed, allowing them to test how evaluation instruments influence honesty assessments. The language model must declare the quest complete, unreachable, or undecidable under a budget, with the engine scoring each verdict based on preregistered decision rules. They found that changes in the evaluation instrument, such as expanding verdict options or disclosing success criteria, significantly altered measured model behavior and verdict distributions, revealing instability and sensitivity to instrument design. The study included multiple series of tests with fixed player behavior but varying instrument configurations, showing that verdict outcomes shifted dramatically depending on the instrument's grammar and narrative register. Some preregistered hypotheses were falsified, while post-hoc analyses suggested that narrative presence and budget rendering influenced verdicts more than content details. The authors propose a four-check integrity protocol to improve the reliability of evaluation instruments in language model honesty assessments.

items.title: SAGA introduces schema-aware grounding to improve agentic text-to-SPARQL generation, achieving top accuracy across nine Wikidata and Freebase benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: SAGA is a training-free framework designed to enhance semantic parsing for complex knowledge base question answering by incorporating schema constraints into property exploration. It maintains a bidirectional type state to filter incompatible properties and presents schema-annotated graph patterns, addressing the common issue of type-blind grounding that leads to semantically incompatible queries and empty results. Evaluated on nine benchmark settings over Wikidata and Freebase, SAGA achieved the highest F1 scores on all and the highest exact-match accuracy on eight, while consistently reducing empty-result queries. This approach improves the interaction between large language model agents and knowledge bases by systematically conditioning on entity types, property domains, ranges, and expected answer types during query generation.

items.title: WrAFT launches modular automated writing evaluation system for argumentative essays using LLMs, achieving state-of-the-art scoring accuracy on TOEFL dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: WrAFT is a new automated writing assessment tool designed to score and provide detailed feedback on argumentative essays. It uses a modular approach separating scoring, surface-level feedback, and deep-level feedback, and evaluates large language models like LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct, GPT-4o, and Claude 3.7 through prompting and fine-tuning. The system was tested on 480 TOEFL Independent Writing essays with official scores, achieving a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.84 and RMSE of 0.44 on a 0-5 scale, indicating strong scoring performance. Human evaluations of the feedback generated by WrAFT showed high approval rates, with over 93% positive ratings for both surface-level and deep-level feedback types. An interactive user interface for the system has been developed and is publicly available for free use, aiming to support writing assessment and feedback in educational contexts.

items.title: SMC-ES algorithm synthesizes control policies with formal safety and robustness guarantees using evolutionary strategies and statistical model checking [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose SMC-ES, a simulation-based method that automatically synthesizes control policies for autonomous cyber-physical systems with formal guarantees on performance, safety, and robustness. The method provides certificates ensuring that, with high confidence, the probability of violating specified properties remains below a given threshold. SMC-ES integrates Evolutionary Strategies with Statistical Model Checking and is evaluated on continuous control tasks using Gymnasium and Safety Gymnasium testbeds. Results indicate that SMC-ES achieves competitive performance against leading model-free Deep Reinforcement Learning baselines while offering formal verification guarantees at a manageable computational cost.

items.title: Researchers evaluate five Atari Pong world models, find failures in ball dynamics and policy performance, and propose Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization to improve modeling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers studied five visual world-model agents in Atari Pong-DreamerV3, DIAMOND, TWISTER, Simulus, and STORM-by freezing their learned models and testing them with separately trained policies. They found consistent failures such as ball disappearance, incorrect motion, and invalid ball-paddle interactions, and observed that policies trained inside frozen models underperformed compared to original training pipelines, with DreamerV3 showing a significant drop in mean return. To address these issues, the team proposed Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization (CGSReg), an auxiliary pixel reconstruction loss focused on segmented concept regions like the ball. Experiments showed that CGSReg improved closed-loop rollouts and zero-shot model-based reinforcement learning performance in some models, though its effects varied and it did not resolve all world-model limitations.

items.title: MedFailBench releases clinician-built synthetic benchmark for medical AI safety boundary failure analysis with severity and error type labels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: MedFailBench introduces an open-source synthetic benchmark designed by clinicians to identify and categorize safety boundary failures in medical AI systems. The benchmark labels errors by severity and type, such as missed urgent escalation and unsafe dosing, aiming to improve AI safety evaluation beyond correctness of answers. The current public version includes 44 clinician-reviewed synthetic cases with severity annotations, a safety gate taxonomy, a clinical severity rubric, and an automated pipeline for archiving model-response screenings. It does not include patient data, clinical validation claims, or model rankings and is released under Apache-2.0 and CC-BY-4.0 licenses.

items.title: Benchmarking six multimodal large language models on scientific visualization literacy reveals uneven performance and highlights Gemini as the strongest model exceeding human average [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers benchmarked six multimodal large language models (MLLMs), including three closed-source and three open-source models, using a standardized scientific visualization literacy assessment with 49 items across 18 visualizations and 11 task types. The evaluation compared model performance to data from 485 human participants, finding that Gemini outperformed the human mean while open-source models lagged behind. Models showed strengths in scientific illustration, search, and spatial understanding but struggled with texture-based visualizations, integration tasks, and quantitative estimation. Error analysis identified common failures in fine-grained quantitative estimation, flow-direction interpretation, and grounded encoding interpretation, underscoring the need to include scientific visualization literacy as a benchmark for multimodal AI systems. The researchers have made their code and model outputs publicly available to support further study and development in this area.

items.title: Researchers demonstrate feasibility of poisoning language model pretraining data via public web discussion interfaces and introduce HalfLife to estimate adversarial content inclusion [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have shown that poisoning attacks on language model pretraining data can be conducted through public discussion interfaces on the web, extending beyond previously studied sources like Wikipedia. They introduce HalfLife, a new method to estimate the presence of malicious content in web-crawled training data after data curation processes. The study highlights the risk posed by third-party webpage content as a vector for injecting harmful data into large-scale language model training corpora, emphasizing the need to assess and mitigate such threats in pretraining pipelines.

items.title: Researchers introduce Just Keep Prompting framework to evaluate Vision-Language Models' stability under repeated Socratic questioning across 720 multi-turn runs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers developed Just Keep Prompting (JKP), a multi-turn evaluation framework to test Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for epistemic stability when repeatedly challenged or questioned. They applied JKP using three prompting strategies on GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Qwen3-VL-30B across a subset of the STAR benchmark, analyzing up to 10 follow-up turns per run. The study found that while aggregate accuracy changed modestly over repeated prompts, individual answer trajectories showed significant instability, including answer flipping and regression of correct responses. Model behavior varied: Qwen3-VL-30B achieved the highest final accuracy but was prone to confident errors under contradiction, Gemini 2.5 Pro was more stable but costly in tokens, and GPT-4o was the most brittle. These results highlight that multi-turn evaluation reveals how VLMs balance visual grounding, calibration, and conversational compliance under sustained challenge.

items.title: Researchers propose LBA, a sampling-based method for textual hard-label adversarial attacks that reduces query costs and improves quality across six language models and four datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce LBA, a new method for generating high-quality adversarial texts under low query budgets in hard-label scenarios. Unlike existing greedy algorithms that substitute text positions sequentially and incur high query costs, LBA constructs an approximate distribution of adversarial examples by integrating prior and posterior knowledge, enabling more effective sampling. This approach addresses the impracticality of exhaustive search over all position combinations in the text. Extensive experiments on six language models, from small to large architectures, across four datasets show that LBA outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on all evaluation metrics. Additionally, assessments using large language models indicate that LBA produces adversarial texts that better preserve semantics and comprehensibility compared to previous methods.

items.title: Researchers propose AGOPS to automatically evolve task-specific prompt guidelines that improve large language model performance by up to 81.7% across reasoning, medical, and coding tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce AGOPS, an automatic method that generates task-specific prompt guidelines by optimizing prompts using large language models and reference answers. This approach addresses the common issue of underspecified user queries that cause significant performance drops in large language models. AGOPS leverages completed task examples to infer missing information such as constraints and context, helping users write clearer prompts that enhance model effectiveness. The study demonstrates that underspecified prompts can reduce task performance by up to 95.3%, and existing prompt optimization techniques struggle to recover this loss. By following AGOPS-generated guidelines, users can regain between 15.5% and 81.7% of performance across benchmarks in mathematical reasoning, medical question answering, and coding tasks, showing consistent improvements over generic, manually created prompt guidelines.

items.title: Researchers introduce Token Time Continuous Diffusion, a continuous-space diffusion language model with per-token timing that improves conditional generation and outperforms discrete models at high speedups [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present Token Time Continuous Diffusion (TTCD), a new language model that operates in continuous space and uses per-token timing to map Gaussian noise deterministically to tokens without further sampling. TTCD avoids inaccuracies from parallel token sampling in discrete models and allows more confident tokens to generate faster, enhancing conditional generation performance. The team trained a 160 million parameter TTCD model on OpenWebText and applied self-distillation, finding that TTCD matches or exceeds the unconditional and conditional generation quality of similar-sized discrete models at high speedups. The approach also showed comparable improvements in solving Sudoku puzzles, demonstrating its broader applicability.

items.title: Polestar introduces drift-aware cache calibration and token commitment to improve inference efficiency of diffusion large language models, boosting accuracy by up to 10.73% and throughput by 3.7x [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Polestar is a training-free inference framework designed to enhance the efficiency of diffusion large language models (dLLMs) by addressing challenges caused by bidirectional attention and token representation drift during decoding. It includes two components: Polestar-Cache, which identifies and refreshes stale KV-cache positions to enable efficient reuse, and Polestar-Commit, which detects sharp drift events to identify tokens ready for commitment. Evaluations on mathematics and coding benchmarks across multiple dLLM families show that Polestar achieves a new state of the art on the accuracy-throughput Pareto frontier, with significant improvements in both accuracy and decoding parallelism compared to existing methods.

items.title: Researchers introduce tool efficiency and marginal tool utility metrics to directly measure and optimize LLM tool use in agent trajectories [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: This paper presents tool efficiency, a new quantitative metric designed to evaluate the rate of useful tool calls within large language model (LLM) agent trajectories. It also introduces marginal tool utility, a per-call metric that identifies whether a tool call contributes to accuracy or can be removed to improve efficiency without loss of performance, determined using an LLM-as-a-Judge approach. Unlike prior work that indirectly measures efficiency via accuracy, this research focuses on direct post hoc analysis of tool use efficiency to aid future benchmark designs and the development of leaner tool suites for LLM agents.

items.title: Study finds baseline prompting outperforms complex techniques in LLM multiple-choice question answering across 10 datasets and 27 model configurations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers conducted a comprehensive empirical study evaluating eight prompting techniques on multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) tasks using 27 large language model configurations and over 4,300 unique questions. The study found that simple baseline prompting consistently outperformed more complex reasoning methods, with only minimal expert and inductive role framing providing a small but statistically significant improvement of about 3 percentage points. Other sophisticated techniques often underperformed, sometimes by large margins. The study also examined three key phenomena: the unexpected top performance of the Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 model in Elo ratings, trade-offs between performance and efficiency across models with varying thinking budgets, and significant variation in dataset difficulty, with 60% of benchmarks scoring below 70% accuracy and a wide accuracy spread indicating room for model improvement. These findings suggest that the LLM evaluation community may be overcomplicating prompt engineering and that focusing on genuine model enhancements could yield better results than optimizing prompts alone.

items.title: Researchers present MAPS framework to model multi-agent dialogue with co-existing subjective perspectives and shared meaning, balancing individual reasoning and semantic alignment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce MAPS (Multi-Agent Perspective Spaces), a framework designed to model dialogue between cognitively distinct agents by maintaining individualized reasoning while enabling convergence on shared meaning. The system uses domain-weighted profiles, dynamic GRU-based memory, and interpretable token-level attention to support diverse and interpretable dialogue. Evaluations on datasets including EmpatheticDialogues, TopicalChat, and MultiWOZ demonstrate that MAPS achieves semantic alignment without collapsing subjectivity, offering a path toward dialogue systems that balance expressiveness and coherence while preserving cognitive diversity.

items.title: Introspection Fine-Tuning (IFT): Training Small LLMs to Introspect [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can small language models detect and report on perturbations their own internal activations? We investigate this question through the lens of activation steering: injecting concept vectors into a model's residual stream and measuring whether the model can accurately report on the perturbation. We first show that the binary detection paradigm used in prior work -- prompting the model to answer Yes'' or No'' to whether it detects an injected thought -- is confounded in small models, as steering biases the model toward affirmative responses regardless of the question content. We therefore propose two confound-free evaluation paradigms: sentence localization (identifying which of $N$ sentences was perturbed, chance $= 1/N$) and strength comparison (identifying which of two sentences received a stronger injection, chance $= 50\%$). Evaluating across six models from two families (Llama-3.2 and Gemma-4), we find that models as small as 2B parameters introspect reliably well above chance, and that introspective ability generally increases with scale. Llama-1B, however, performs at or below chance. We then introduce \emph{Introspection Fine-Tuning} (IFT): supervised fine-tuning on sentence-localization examples constructed from the model's own perturbed forward passes. IFT raises Llama-1B sentence-localization accuracy from $9.6\%$ to $60.6\%$ (a $6\times$ improvement), with gains generalizing zero-shot to the held-out strength-comparison task ($30.2\% \to 52.2\%$). IFT also improves introspection for 3B and 8B models, while inducing negligible degradation on standard capability benchmarks. Our results suggest that introspective ability is not fixed by scale alone: it can be directly trained, and doing so unlocks latent self-monitoring capacity with implications for AI transparency and alignment. Our code is \href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/IFT-introspection-2092/README.md}{here}.

items.title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Reliability and Scaling in Language Models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are evaluated as though perfect reliability is achievable for any task given sufficient scale. We show this assumption is information-theoretically unjustified. Every generative task has a reliability ceiling that no model can exceed, determined by how much output uncertainty is resolvable from observable context. The gap decomposes into a resolvable component closable with additional context and a subjective component inherent to task ambiguity. Autoregressive generation further degrades this ceiling at a rate governed by the task's dependency kernel, which quantifies inter-token correlations in the output. From these two primitives, we derive a first-principles scaling law where LLM performance is bottlenecked by the scarcer resource: training data or model capacity. This law recovers the Chinchilla scaling law as a special case and provides a structural account of when scaling improves reliability. Beyond scaling, our framework unifies diverse practical phenomena, such as the benefits of retrieval-augmentation and the spectral mechanics of catastrophic forgetting. Our work formalizes the resource-complexity tradeoffs that govern model performance across domains, offering a unified theory of performance limits in generative language models.

items.title: T5-CSBoost: Adversarial Perturbation Resistant LLM Fingerprinting [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While many AI-generated text (AIGT) detectors achieve strong performance on clean inputs, their accuracy degrades significantly under light paraphrasing, word substitutions, character edits, and distribution shifts. We present T5 Contrastive Style Boosted Classifier (T5-CSBoost), an extension to the T5-Sentinel framework that keeps the original next-token prediction objective for source attribution while introducing an auxiliary margin-based triplet loss over decoder embeddings. This contrastive style regularization encourages the learning of compact, perturbation-resistant stylistic representations, offering a lightweight yet effective alternative to prior approaches that rely on architectural modifications, adversarial training, or complex multi-task objectives without altering the underlying T5-small backbone. T5-CSBoost achieves state-of-the-art multiclass source attribution and binary human-vs-LLM detection on OpenLLMText and HC3 AIGT benchmarks. More importantly, T5-CSBoost demonstrates enhanced robustness to word and character level adversarial perturbations of up to 90% intensity, achieving state-of-the-art on the challenging MAGE/Deepfake stress-test suite, including unseen models, unseen domains, and extreme paraphrasing scenarios. Our results highlight that explicitly regularizing stylistic embeddings via contrastive learning is a practical and effective strategy for building more robust LLM fingerprinting systems in real-world adversarial settings.

items.title: CoEvoT: Co-Evolving Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Graph-LLM Reasoning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph learning under distribution shift presents a persistent challenge, where models adapt to new graphs with limited or even no supervision. Recent graph--LLM approaches move toward label-efficient prediction by linearizing graphs into prompts and using large language models (LLMs) as predictors, and can adopt Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to exploit LLM's multi-step reasoning capability. However, existing CoT-based graph--LLM methods generate intermediate thoughts while conditioning on fixed graph tokens, limiting step-wise refinement of structural cues. In this paper, we propose CoEvoT, a simple yet effective co-evolving CoT prompting framework for graph--LLM reasoning. CoEvoT couples text-to-graph token rewriting and graph-to-text reasoning guidance in a closed loop: each intermediate textual thought is used to update the graph token evidence state via a lightweight condition network, and the updated tokens are fed back into the next-step instruction to guide subsequent LLM reasoning. This enables step-wise, state-aware evidence refinement, rather than reasoning over a fixed graph snapshot. Extensive experiments on eight datasets demonstrate that CoEvoT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

items.title: ReportMedSAM: Guiding Segmentation Through Radiology Reports [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Free-form radiology reports contain rich clinical descriptions, yet converting them for reliable segmentation remains challenging due to the inherent variability of natural language. Existing pipelines often rely on predefined organ phrases or brittle rule-based inference-time extraction, which limits their scalability to novel anatomical structures and makes them sensitive to linguistic variations. To address this, we propose ReportMedSAM, a report-driven framework that replaces discrete extraction with a learnable concept bank. By leveraging a frozen medical vision-language encoder (BiomedCLIP), we align organ-level concept embeddings with large-scale clinical corpora through contrastive learning, establishing mutually orthogonal semantic anchors. Our approach explicitly mitigates organ-level semantic collapse and ensures high robustness against diverse clinical synonyms (e.g., "renal" vs. "kidney" ). During inference, a clinical report is embedded and matched against this concept bank to dynamically activate task-specific Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules. This decoupled design allows new concepts and experts to be added without retraining existing components, providing a parameter-isolated extension mechanism while keeping previously learned experts unchanged. Evaluated on the AbdomenAtlas 3.0 dataset, ReportMedSAM effectively interprets free-form reports, achieves competitive segmentation accuracy, and demonstrates seamless, non-interfering extension to novel clinical tasks.

items.title: Heterogeneous Element-Aware Cross-Version Differencing of Scientific Documents via Layout-Aware Alignment and Structure-Aware Reasoning
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-version differencing of scientific documents is essential in scholarly publishing and technical documentation, but remains challenging because scientific documents are page-structured artifacts containing heterogeneous elements such as text, tables, formulas, figures, and layout cues. Existing text-sequence-based methods often lose layout and structural information, while image-based methods lack semantic interpretability and are sensitive to rendering variation. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a layout-aware heterogeneous element-aware framework for scientific document differencing. The framework decomposes document versions into semantically typed elements, establishes cross-version correspondence through an alignment-first mechanism that jointly models spatial, content, and structural compatibility, and performs type-aware difference reasoning over aligned element pairs. It supports unified change detection, localization, structure-awareness analysis, and alignment/matching evaluation across text, tables, formulas, and figures. Experiments on real-world scientific PDF data from journal production proofreading workflows show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms element-specific baselines. It achieves detection F1 scores of 0.903, 0.855, 0.862, and 0.845 for text, tables, formulas, and figures, respectively, with further improvements in localization, structure awareness, and matching quality. Ablation and sensitivity analyses confirm the effectiveness of cross-version alignment, type-specific representations, structure-aware reasoning, and compatibility-weight design. These results demonstrate that heterogeneous element-aware differencing provides a robust and interpretable solution for scientific document comparison in realistic editorial production scenarios.

items.title: Position: Explainability Research Must Prioritize Foundations over Ad-hoc Methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite the proliferation of Explainable AI (XAI) techniques -- from feature attributions to sparse autoencoders -- explanations rarely influence real-world workflows. In practice, they are often generated and discarded without guiding meaningful action. This gap reflects foundational shortcomings: research has not yet established methodologies for integrating explanations into end-to-end, human-in-the-loop systems. This position paper argues that the machine learning community must pivot from ad-hoc XAI methods toward addressing foundational & structural challenges, including unclear problem formulations, underspecified evaluation objectives, and the absence of pipelines for explanation-driven feedback. We support this claim through an analysis of recent ICML, NeurIPS, and ICLR papers and a survey of XAI practitioners, revealing recurring issues that limit cumulative progress. We conclude by outlining a practical checklist designed to shift XAI toward a more human-centered, action-oriented paradigm. By emphasizing foundational clarity over the development of ad-hoc methods, we hope to provide a roadmap for integrating explanations into actionable, feedback-driven AI systems.

items.title: Explainable Geospatial AI for Satellite Ground Station Siting Using LiDAR-Derived Terrain Intelligence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Representative clutter height (RCH) is a key parameter in radio propagation and interference analysis because it captures the dominant height of local obstructions that drive terminal clutter loss. Current practice often relies on fixed clutter heights assigned to land use classes in Recommendation ITU-R P.452-18, but this misses within class variation and can lead to conservative exclusion zones and poor site ranking for low Earth orbit ground station siting and spectrum coordination. We present an interpretable, globally deployable machine learning framework for predicting RCH from open geospatial data. The model is trained using LiDAR derived labels from the U.S. Geological Survey 3D Elevation Program and inference time features from global land-cover, terrain, demographic, thermal, and optical remote sensing products. We define RCH using a robust 75th percentile clutter height statistic, evaluate multiple regressors, and select LightGBM for its accuracy, efficiency, and compatibility with feature attribution analysis. The final model achieves a mean absolute error of 1.79m and an R^2=0.765, reducing absolute error by more than 60% relative to the ITU baseline. Beyond aggregate fit, we evaluate domain facing criteria relevant to RF planning, including meter scale error, tolerance band accuracy, over and under estimation tails, agreement with ITU clutter height regimes, and SHAP-based physical plausibility. SHAP identifies tree canopy cover, land-cover semantics, and spectral reflectance as the most influential predictors. Studies on segmentation derived features, non-forest ablations, and land-cover matched international validation show that open geospatial data can improve clutter modeling at scale without sacrificing interpretability or deployability.

items.title: The Planar Case of Thomas Positive Circuits Conjecture
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The notion of circuit refers to a cyclic oriented influence between the elements of a dynamical system. There are two classes of circuit: positive and negative. R. Thomas conjectured that a necessary condition of multi stationarity is the existence of positive circuits. In this paper we use dynamical system tools and planar analysis to find conditions for which the conjecture holds for planar systems.

items.title: Certified Domain Consistency for Multi-Domain Retrieval: Label-Free Per-Domain Contamination Control with Conformal Risk Guarantees [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval over corpora that mix several domains often returns relevant but wrong-domain evidence that ranking metrics miss and that conformal risk control bounds only marginally, under-covering the worst domains. This work introduces C3R, a drop-in control layer that, from an inferred domain posterior and no query-time label, certifies a per-domain contamination budget where feasible and otherwise abstains rather than silently violating; on the hardest domains it guarantees a reduction, not a tight bound. The core is a two-split scheme built on risk-controlling prediction sets, whose finite-sample transfer bound crosses from the inferred to the true domain with fully estimable slack, supports heterogeneous budgets, and inverts for deployment. Population validity rests on this bound and a controlled simulation; across a thousand resampled calibrations the certificate never violates (a stability result) while marginal control violates the most-contaminated domain in every draw, and soft demotion retains more recall than the strongest calibrated cascade at equal certified contamination. The method replicates across open testbeds including an independent one from public federal regulations, and an LLM-judged downstream probe indicates wrong-authority grounding rises with contamination and falls under control. The layer is frozen-stack and reranker-agnostic.

items.title: Towards Reliable AI-Assisted Analog Design: Template-Constrained LLM Agents for SAR ADC Generation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14165v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant capability in software code generation, their application to analog Electronic Design Automation (EDA) is bottlenecked. Owing to limited circuit topology understanding and data, directly prompting LLMs and multimodal models leads to hallucinations and failure to produce schematics capable of passing rigorous SPICE simulations, as we show in our work. Instead, we propose an end-to-end, multi-step LLM agentic framework ATLAS, capable of generating a functional Successive Approximation Register (SAR) Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) that successfully passes simulation validation. To adhere to the rigid constraints of analog design, we utilize expert knowledge to ground the LLM in its planning, selection, parameterization, and iterative modification. As part of ATLAS, we introduce Template-Constrained Generation - which unlike other template-based works - builds towards a more generalized SAR ADC generation flow. We demonstrate a strong proof-of-concept of our framework by developing SAR ADCs across technology nodes and input specs. Overall, our expert-knowledge grounded multi-step agentic ATLAS establishes a pragmatic foundation for integrating LLMs into reliable analog design methodologies.

items.title: RENEW: Towards Learning World Models and Repairing Model Exploitation from Preferences [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models are widely used in offline reinforcement learning (RL) to improve sample efficiency and generate experience beyond a fixed dataset. However, they are vulnerable to model exploitation where data coverage is thin. Prior work addresses this either by collecting more expert demonstrations, which is often expensive, unsafe, or unavailable, or by conservative algorithms that avoid uncertain regions, which limits generalization. We propose instead to repair exploitation directly using human preferences over imagined rollouts, leveraging the strong intuitive physics that allows humans to easily spot egregious dynamics hallucinations. We formalize this as Dynamics Learning from Human Feedback (DLHF), a Bradley-Terry preference loss over trajectory log-likelihoods under a learned dynamics model. Unfortunately, naive DLHF is sample inefficient, so we introduce RENEW, which uses epistemic uncertainty to focus finetuning where the model is most exploitable. We evaluate on several Jumanji and classic control environments and find that while naive DLHF requires an outsize preference budget, RENEW makes the framework practical by improving sample efficiency, limiting catastrophic forgetting, and reducing exploitation in pretrained world models. Taken together, our results provide initial evidence that preferences can supervise world model dynamics directly, offering a new approach to addressing exploitation in offline model-based RL.

items.title: Closed-Loop Knowledge Dynamics: An Operational Framework for Saturation and Escape [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feedback-driven loops support iterative improvement in large language models, reinforcement learning, and autonomous discovery, yet their gains often diminish under repeated internal feedback. We study why closed-loop knowledge systems saturate and what external information can move them beyond their current attractors. We introduce a three-level operational framework in which knowledge states $x_t$ evolve through transition kernels $K_{\theta}$ indexed by a structural parameter $\theta$. The governing structure is defined as the observational equivalence class of $\theta$ induced by these kernels, while attractors and basins are properties of the fixed-$\theta$ dynamics. A structural intervention changes $\theta$ and produces a detectable kernel discrepancy on pre-specified probe states, making structural change falsifiable. Using a Lyapunov drift condition, we show that stable internal dynamics approach bounded stability regions with exponentially attenuated transients and a noise-controlled residual floor. We characterize escape through a metric condition on intervention-induced attractor displacement and a baseline-relative KL lower bound for increasing escape probability. This analysis also explains why conditional mutual information alone cannot certify escape: it measures variation among intervention-conditioned updates rather than departure from the no-intervention law. Case studies in LLM code repair, sparse-reward reinforcement learning, and Bayesian optimization use matched continuation controls to illustrate how feedback strength and alignment affect quality-improving escape. Our contribution is an operational connection among stability tools, measurable intervention effects, and cross-domain diagnostics.

items.title: NexForge: Scaling Executable Agent Tasks via Requirement-First Synthesis [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14186v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling executable agent training data is bottlenecked by substrate-first methods that tie task generation to predefined tools, repositories, or skill graphs: expanding coverage requires manual expansion of the substrate, each new domain demands a bespoke pipeline, and the resulting task distributions often reflect substrate convenience rather than real-world demand. We introduce NexForge, a requirement-first framework that compiles free-form capability requirements into executable agent training data. NexForge first performs research-based demand discovery to identify representative task forms, realistic scenarios, and their relative prevalence. It then applies distribution-aware task compilation and automatically retrieves or constructs the files, repositories, dependencies, and runtime configurations required to materialize each task, followed by teacher rollout collection and trajectory distillation. The same pipeline, without any domain-specific infrastructure, produces 3,600 terminal tasks and 2,000 office tasks, improving Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Base from 22.5% to 52.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and from 813 to 1338 Elo on GDPval; scaling to 43.2K terminal tasks reaches 58.4%, surpassing Claude Opus 4.6. Scaled further, NexForge-synthesized data contributes to the training of Nex-N2, a family of publicly available agent models that lift Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to 75.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and to 1585 Elo on GDPval -- achieving state-of-the-art open-source performance and surpassing several frontier proprietary systems. Nex-N2 models are available at https://nex.sii.edu.cn/

items.title: LIGO-PINN: Learned Initialization via Gated Optimization to Alleviate Convergence Failures in Physics Informed Neural Networks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have had a broad research impact in modeling domains governed by partial differential equations (PDE). However, PINNs have been shown to perform poorly, sometimes even converging to trivial solutions, in challenging PDE domains, or when generalizing to unseen but related PDE domains. Previously proposed solutions detail hyperparameter tuning to reduce loss imbalance between data-driven and physics guided losses, curriculum learning based training strategies, or dynamic re-sampling of hard collocation points. These methods face certain pitfalls: hyperparameter tuning is expensive, designing a training curriculum is ambiguous in multi-parameter PDE settings, and dynamic resampling still fails in complex PDE settings. Complementary to this line of thinking, we believe the initial PINN network weights also play a crucial role in the emergence of catastrophic failures during training, yet the effect of PINN weight initialization has been surprisingly under-investigated. To this end, we propose a framework for Learned Initialization via Gated Layerwise Optimization (LIGO-PINN) to overcome PINN convergence failures. Through rigorous evaluation on 1D and 2D PDE domains, including a challenging 2D fluid dynamics setting, we demonstrate that our methodology outperforms state-of-the-art methods designed to alleviate PINN failures, achieving a 91.5% average performance improvement across six baselines and 81% over the strongest baseline. We also verify that LIGO-PINN generalizes to 3D unstructured domains. Finally, we analyze training dynamics across all three PDE domains to explain both LIGO-PINN's improvement and the convergence failure of traditional PINNs. Code: https://github.com/scailab/ligo-pinn Keywords: Machine Learning, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, Deep Learning, PDE Modeling

items.title: Never Too Late for Force: Accelerating VLA Post-Training with Reactive Force Injection [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies provide strong language-conditioned manipulation knowledge, but they remain largely vision-driven and can struggle once manipulation enters contact states where the scene is occluded, depth is ambiguous, or small force errors push execution off the offline demonstration distribution. We present LIFT (Late Reactive Injection of Force for VLA Post-Training), a force-aware post-training framework that adds contact reactivity to a pretrained VLA policy while preserving its general manipulation knowledge. LIFT grafts a reactive action expert beside the original action expert, initializes it from pretrained action weights, and injects recent 6D end-effector force through causal force memory and zero-initialized cross attention, enabling actions to be refreshed during execution. To address the policy-dependent distribution shift of contact feedback, LIFT further couples reactive force injection with an online DAgger loop that trains on a mixture of offline task-alignment data and human-corrected online rollouts. Across towel folding, book insertion, and Hanoi ring placement, LIFT learns faster and reaches higher performance than vision-only post-training, while ablations show that reactive force memory and online corrective data are both important for robust contact-rich manipulation. Our code and data will be publicly available.

items.title: MEMORA: Embodied Action Memory from Egocentric Videos for Reasoning and Planning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2607.14252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon robot planning requires more than predicting what actions will do next; it also requires memory of the embodied experience that makes future goals interpretable. People do not plan from the present scene alone: they draw on remembered places, object-state changes, prior procedures, and regularities revealed through repeated action. We formulate Embodied Action Memory (EAM) as the capability to form, maintain, and use such experience as a persistent memory state for later decisions. MEMORA realizes EAM with a formation-consolidation-retrieval lifecycle and four typed stores: Environment Memory, Entity Memory, Activity Memory, and Inferred Knowledge. Online editing maintains object identities and state histories as new observations arrive; offline consolidation abstracts repeated experience into reusable procedures and participant-specific regularities. MEMORA-Bench evaluates this lifecycle on 45 hours of EPIC-KITCHENS-100 extension video across 18 participants through memory-grounded planning, including previously unseen goals, and a complementary memory-assessment task. Across four open-weight language models, full MEMORA--combining editing, typed stores, and consolidation--achieves the strongest aggregate results among the evaluated memory conditions. It improves memory-assessment accuracy by up to 20.5 points over the strongest controlled baseline and improves out-of-distribution Robot-Grounded Plan score by up to 16.6% relative. A qualitative two-task robot deployment study further illustrates how memory-grounded language plans can interface with downstream control, while the overall results show that editable, consolidated memory can supply remembered context for robot planning. Project page: https://yuzihaowashu.github.io/MEMORA/
